edits.new: - The finite-substratum scope of Theorem 23 supplies the two steps that have no established form for a substratum of unspecified cardinality. The first is Stage 1's exact rooted return $\Gamma_n=I$ after a non-permutation rooted map. The step from such a return to P-indivisibility holds for a hidden prior on a measurable hidden carrier of any cardinality (Corollary (near-return) of [Main §2.3], of which an exact return is a case), and the near-return condition (NR) of [Main §2.3], assumed and not adopted, is a weaker sufficient condition for that conclusion (§3.2); what is open for a substratum of unspecified cardinality is a source of the return hypothesis. The second is Stage 3's count under H-count, which [GR §2.3] states for a total system that is finite. E3 does not establish finiteness of $S$. An effective-finiteness argument with continuum UV completion is not developed. Theorem 23 retains its stated finite-substratum hypothesis. Its Stage 2 local lattice results are also stated on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ under their named hypotheses [SM §4.1]; the observer-operator pole statement of Lemma 1c [SM §4.1] and the continued response of Proposition 4b [SM §4.4] additionally need, outside the finite and translation-invariant cases of [SM §4.1], a meromorphic continuation of the memory-resummed Schur complement that is not established. These do not by themselves extend the complete reconstruction theorem to a substratum of unspecified cardinality.

E3, read as a Hilbert-space dimension cutoff $\dim\mathcal H\le e^{A/4}$, bounds the observationally relevant visible sector and boundary layer $\mathcal C_V\times\mathcal C_B$ under the deep-sector influence bound H-BD of [GR §3.2]. Theorem 24(iii) gives an exact freedom to adjoin independently prepared decoupled factors of any cardinality at a fixed interface, each in a normalized state or law with its own unitary, isometric or measurable dynamics; an unnormalizable factor is not covered. A deep sector coupled under H-BD changes the transition law by at most $2t/\tau_{BD}$ ([GR §3.2]), so its comparison is only at leading order on accessible timescales.
